## 🔴 Errors (likely broken or will cause build failures / incorrect behavior)

### 🔴 E1 — `$(TargetFramework)` condition in `.props` is dead code (AP-21)
**File:** `Directory.Build.props`, line 10

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** For single-targeting projects (all projects in this repo target only `net8.0`), `$(TargetFramework)` is **empty** during `.props` evaluation. The SDK sets it after `Directory.Build.props` is imported. This condition **never matches**, so `GenerateDocumentationFile` is silently never set.

**Fix:** Move this conditional block to `Directory.Build.targets`, which is imported *after* the SDK populates `$(TargetFramework)`:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.targets -->
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(TargetFramework)' == 'net8.0'">
  <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E2 — Property defaults in `.targets` silently override project-level settings
**File:** `Directory.Build.targets`, lines 6–11

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors>true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

**Problem:** `Directory.Build.targets` is evaluated **after** individual `.csproj` files. Any properties set here unconditionally will **override** project-level values. Specifically, `LibB.csproj` (line 13) sets `<TreatWarningsAsErrors>false</TreatWarningsAsErrors>`, but this `.targets` file stomps it back to `true`. LibB has no way to opt out.

**Fix:** Move these to `Directory.Build.props` so they act as *defaults* that projects can override, or add a guard condition:

```xml
<!-- In Directory.Build.props (preferred — acts as default) -->
<PropertyGroup>
  <TreatWarningsAsErrors Condition="'$(TreatWarningsAsErrors)' == ''">true</TreatWarningsAsErrors>
  <Company>Contoso</Company>
  <Authors>Build Team</Authors>
  <Copyright>Copyright 2024 Contoso</Copyright>
</PropertyGroup>
```

---

### 🔴 E3 — `DefineConstants` is overwritten instead of appended
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 14

```xml
<DefineConstants>ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

**Problem:** This **replaces** all existing constants. The SDK defines `TRACE` (and `DEBUG` in Debug configuration) by default. After this line, those are gone — code guarded by `#if TRACE` or `#if DEBUG` silently stops executing.

**Fix:** Append to the existing value:

```xml
<DefineConstants>$(DefineConstants);ENABLE_LOGGING</DefineConstants>
```

---

### 🔴 E4 — Unquoted condition on `$(Configuration)`
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, line 13

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="$(Configuration) == Debug">
```

**Problem:** The condition value is not quoted. If `$(Configuration)` is empty (e.g., during NuGet restore or design-time builds), this evaluates to ` == Debug` which is a malformed expression causing `MSB4100` or an evaluation error.

**Fix:** Always single-quote both sides of MSBuild conditions:

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(Configuration)' == 'Debug'">
```

---

### 🔴 E5 — Publish-on-build target re-invokes the project, causing double-build and potential file race
**File:** `LibA/LibA.csproj`, lines 43–45

```xml
<Target Name="PublishOnBuild" AfterTargets="Build">
  <MSBuild Projects="$(MSBuildProjectFullPath)" Targets="Publish" Properties="_IsPublishing=true" />
</Target>
```

**Problem:** This spawns a **second evaluation** of the same project with an extra global property (`_IsPublishing=true`). Both instances write to the same `OutputPath` / `IntermediateOutputPath`, creating a race condition. This doubles build time and can cause intermittent failures with "file in use" errors.

**Fix:** If publish-on-build is required, use `DependsOnTargets` to run Publish within the same project instance:

```xml
<PropertyGroup Condition="'$(PublishOnBuild)' == 'true'">
  <BuildDependsOn>$(BuildDependsOn);Publish</BuildDependsOn>
</PropertyGroup>
```

### 🔴 E6 — F# compile order is wrong in `BrokenOrder.fsproj`

<Compile Include="Services.fs" />
